dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: Concrete two-sided problem: graphical editors are unusable for people who can't operate a mouse or see a canvas (alt-text ends at reading; no one can EDIT by conversation), and the WebMCP challenge judges reward entries where page-embedded tools are essential — a canvas whose scene graph is readable and editable through tools is a literal 'screen reader that can write back'.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Four measurable goals: second Devpost submission before 2026-09-03 13:00 PT, ≥14 WebMCP tools including a describe_canvas ↔ edit round-trip, a one-prompt multi-operation edit in ChatGPT desktop, and a <3min video demonstrating eyes-free editing.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: 5 command-checkable criteria mirroring the verified Loopmate set (build, pinned vitest tool-surface suite, registerTool grep, curl -sf against the already-claimed speakeasel.netlify.app, LICENSE) plus 4 named judgment checks (filmed one-prompt edit, filmed describe-after-human-edit round-trip, video <3:00, Devpost receipt).

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: MVP locked to Fabric.js-backed primitives (load/upload image, adjustments via built-in filters, crop, rotate, text objects, object move/remove, undo/redo, PNG export) with a ~15-tool surface; layers UI, drawing tools, mobile, accounts, AI image generation explicitly out; dynamic per-object tools and keyboard-shortcut overlay stretch.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: The known tension — a credible editor in ~24h — was surfaced with an explicit Execution-risk score (5/10) before the user chose this idea over the recommended alternative; mitigation (Fabric.js instead of from-scratch, generated sample scene instead of licensed assets, reuse of Loopmate's proven scaffold/deploy/test patterns) is recorded as decisions.

problem: Graphical editing is the least accessible category of software: if you can't operate a mouse precisely or can't see the canvas, image editors are simply closed to you. Assistive tech stops at reading — alt text describes an image, but nothing lets a person hear what is on a canvas and then change it. The blind parent who wants to crop and caption a family photo has no path at all.

This is also a thesis entry for the WebMCP Challenge (deadline 2026-09-03 13:00 PT; judged on WebMCP Leverage, Execution, Potential Impact, Creativity): when an editor's full scene graph is exposed as readable AND writable page tools, the agent in the browser becomes the interface — 'a screen reader that can write back.' The photo also never leaves the tab: the agent operates local state through tools, which no server-side API can replicate. Second, substantially different submission alongside Loopmate (rules permit multiple entries).

mvp.item: Fabric.js canvas hosting one background image + text/shape objects, with a generated sample scene (gradient + shapes) and drag-drop/file-upload image loading
mvp.reason: Fabric's object model, filters, and JSON serialization make a credible editor buildable in hours; generated sample avoids all asset licensing; upload keeps photos local to the tab

mvp.item: Edit operations: brightness/contrast/saturation adjustments (Fabric filters), crop, rotate, add/edit/move/remove text objects, undo/redo history, PNG export
mvp.reason: The minimum operation set for a believable 'edit a photo by talking' demo, each mapping 1:1 to a tool; goal 3's demo prompt needs exactly these

mvp.item: ~14 WebMCP tools including get_canvas_state (scene graph JSON), describe_canvas (prose scene narration — the a11y thesis tool), and a statically registered undo that answers 'nothing to undo' when history is empty
mvp.reason: The judged artifact; describe_canvas is the manifesto ('a screen reader that can write back'); undo is static per critic review — dynamic lifecycle is stretch flex, not MVP machinery
Carried from Loopmate where it passed review: agent actions become legible on camera, and for this entry it doubles as visible evidence for sighted viewers of what the eyes-free user hears

mvp.item: Accessible page shell: keyboard-operable chrome (toolbar, object-list panel, dialogs, focus states), ARIA labels/roles; the object-list panel mirrors the scene graph
mvp.reason: An a11y-framed entry with an inaccessible page would be judged a fraud; keyboard manipulation of canvas objects themselves is stretch — the thesis demo drives edits through the agent, not arrow keys

mvp.item: Netlify deploy via REST script (site pre-claimed: speakeasel.netlify.app) + public GitHub repo with OSS license + README carrying the a11y thesis and tool walkthrough
mvp.reason: Hard submission requirements; deploy path proven on Loopmate

decisions.decision: Build a second, substantially different entry rather than replacing or deepening Loopmate
decisions.rejected: Deepening Loopmate with the selected upgrades (living FX registry, declarative form tool, share-link); replacing Loopmate entirely
decisions.reason: Devpost rules allow multiple submissions per entrant; Loopmate is finished and verified, so a second entry doubles top-10 shots at the cost of extra filming, while a replacement would gamble a done entry on a 24h build.
User chose the manifesto play with the Execution risk (5/10 in a 24h window) explicitly stated; impact narrative is the strongest of the three and lands with the Chrome judge.

decisions.rejected: From-scratch canvas editor; Konva; embedding a hosted editor
decisions.reason: Fabric ships the object model, image filters, transforms, and JSON serialization (get_canvas_state nearly free) under MIT; from-scratch cannot reach credible in 24h, and a hosted editor breaks the local-first story.

decisions.decision: Generated sample scene instead of bundled photos
decisions.reason: Zero licensing risk and zero asset pipeline; user uploads provide real photos at demo time, which also feeds the 'your photo never leaves the tab' line.

decisions.decision: Editor architecture split: a Fabric-free scene-state layer (tools + Node tests run the real thing) and a thin Fabric renderer (browser-only subscriber)
decisions.rejected: Tools calling a canvas-manager interface backed by a behavioral fake in tests; tools importing Fabric directly
decisions.reason: Critic review: a behavioral fake reimplements the editor and tests verify the fake, not the product. The scene/renderer split is the exact store/Tone division that passed review on Loopmate — Node tests exercise real product logic, the renderer just draws state.

decisions.decision: Undo registers statically in MVP; AbortSignal dynamic lifecycle is stretch
decisions.reason: Two critics flagged it: no goal requires lifecycle machinery, it's new unproven state-sync in a 24h build, and it muddies the ≥14-count assertion. Static undo answers 'nothing to undo' when history is empty.

decisions.decision: Blur/grayscale/sepia demoted to the Full tier as the defined cut line
decisions.reason: Critic review: no goal or demo prompt uses them and the tool count survives without them — a 24h build needs a named droppable tier, not an empty one.

decisions.decision: Netlify site pre-claimed and protection pre-disabled at contract time
decisions.reason: Loopmate learning applied: probe external dependencies before execution — the hostname is pinned in the curl criterion from the start and the free-tier team-only 401 cannot recur.

decisions.decision: Reuse Loopmate's proven patterns: dual-surface WebMCP adapter, REST zip-deploy script, shim-backed vitest suite, activity feed
decisions.reason: Every pattern was reviewed and verified green yesterday; reuse converts the 24h risk into mostly-known work.

phases.title: Walking skeleton
phases.notes: FIRST action: npm install fabric + render the sample scene — probing the one new dependency through the WorkOS Socket firewall, the same external system that silently broke the Netlify CLI (already pre-probed green: fabric 7.4.0 installs and imports; specs target the v7 API). Then Vite+TS scaffold (Loopmate patterns), dual-surface adapter + one hello tool, REST deploy to the pre-claimed site via scripts/deploy.sh (prereq: token at ~/.netlify/token, already in place). Risk medium not high: every pipeline unknown was retired yesterday.

phases.notes: Canvas manager over Fabric: image load (upload/drag-drop/sample), filter adjustments, crop, rotate, text objects, object move/remove, undo/redo snapshots, PNG export; toolbar + object-list panel + keyboard operability. The credibility phase — where the 24h risk lives.

phases.title: Tool surface
phases.notes: ~14 tools over the scene-state layer, describe_canvas prose narration, static undo, activity feed, shim vitest suite at the pinned path test/tool-surface.test.ts running the real scene layer. The Leverage criterion lives here.
